The Detroit Youth Arts Alliance (DYAA) requests $90,000 from the Hartwell Foundation over a two-year grant period in support of creative youth development programming for Detroit youth ages 10-18. DYAA is a Midtown Detroit nonprofit serving 400+ youth annually, primarily from underserved Detroit neighborhoods, with after-school and summer programming across five disciplines: visual arts, music, spoken word, dance, and filmmaking. The organization runs on a 14-person full-time staff, including a program director, six teaching artists, three coordinators, two administrators, and a development director, working from the renovated warehouse on Cass Avenue. The $850,000 annual operating budget draws roughly 60% from grants, 20% from individual donors, 15% from events, and 5% from fees. ## Program Description: Creative Youth Development
Hartwell funds would deepen DYAA's core creative youth development model: sustained, artist-led studio programming in which young people build technical skill, voice, and public presentation experience across the five program areas, culminating each year in the Annual Youth Arts Showcase. Programming runs at the Cass Avenue facility today. A second site on Livernois Avenue is under construction, with renovation funded by the Greenfield Foundation's restricted grant ($28,000 renovation budget) and a grand opening scheduled for November 21, 2026; at the time of the November 7 site visit the Livernois site will not yet be open, and this application makes no claim otherwise.
